Learning-Based Dynamic Modeling of an AUV
Phase 1 Comprehensive Report & Presentation Dossier: Hydrodynamics, EDA, and Deep Residual GRU Networks
Robotics Semester 5 Project | Platform: Autosub6000 (AURORA Mission M86) | Status: Complete & Verified

Executive Summary

Autonomous Underwater Vehicles (AUVs) operating in open-ocean survey missions experience intricate hydrodynamic coupling, hydrodynamic damping scaling quadratically with surge speed, and variable wave and current disturbances. Analytical rigid-body physics equations often fail to capture unmodeled thruster deadbands, control-surface actuation delays, and ocean drift, causing cumulative path tracking errors during long-range deployments.

In Phase 1 of this project, we designed, implemented, and thoroughly evaluated a Hybrid Physics-AI Modeling Framework using 31,944 telemetry samples logged at 0.50 Hz (Δt = 2.0 s) by the Autosub6000 AUV during AURORA Mission M86. Rather than relying on a black-box deep learning model, our approach combines a reduced-order 3D marine kinematics baseline with a 2-Layer Recurrent Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) that predicts step-wise residual dynamics: R(t) = Xactual(t+1) − Xphysics(t+1).

Key Finding: Major Dynamic State Error Reductions
Evaluated strictly on 4,792 unseen future test samples, the Hybrid Physics+GRU network achieved substantial error reductions over pure physics kinematics: Pitch Angle RMSE improved by 15.48%, Depth RMSE improved by 12.45%, and Heading Angle RMSE improved by 12.03%. Autoregressive multi-step trajectory simulations confirm that the hybrid formulation maintains physical stability over extended prediction horizons, overcoming the divergence flaws of pure ML models.

1. Dataset Specifications & Zero-Leakage Splitting

The telemetry dataset originates from Autosub6000 Mission M86 (IEEE DataPort). Sensor data was logged at regular 2.0-second intervals from an Inertial Measurement Unit (IMU), Doppler Velocity Log (DVL), acoustic pressure depth sensors, and an Ultra-Short Baseline (USBL) acoustic transceiver.

  • Sampling Frequency: 0.50 Hz (Δt = 2.00 s), with 0% temporal gaps in navigation records.
  • Cleaned Volume: 31,944 verified continuous time-series rows.
  • Chronological Partitioning: Strict time-ordered split (70% Train / 15% Validation / 15% Test) with an 8-point data integrity audit guaranteeing zero future leakage.

3. Reduced-Order Hydrodynamic Physics Model

The baseline physics model couples 3D marine kinematics with quadratic surge hydrodynamic drag over a 2.0-second step:

  • North Position: xt+1 = xt + Ut cos(θt) cos(ψt) Δt
  • East Position: yt+1 = yt + Ut cos(θt) sin(ψt) Δt
  • Operating Depth: zt+1 = zt − Ut sin(θt) Δt
  • Surge Speed: Ut+1 = max(Ut + Kd (Ucruise2 − Ut2) Δt, 0.0)

System Identification: By applying linear least-squares regression to the training split with nominal cruise speed Ucruise = 1.20 m/s, the surge drag coefficient was identified as Kd = 0.022498.

4. Machine Learning Residual Architecture (GRU)

The AI model is structured as a 2-Layer Recurrent Gated Recurrent Unit (GRU) with an MLP decoder:

  • Input Vector (6D): st = [Ut, φt, θt, cos(ψt), sin(ψt), zt]T. Heading is represented trigonometrically to avoid angular wrap discontinuities.
  • Sequence Length: 10 timesteps (20.0 seconds of rolling dynamic memory).
  • Recurrent Core: 2 GRU layers with 64 hidden units each.
  • Decoder: Linear(64 → 32) → ReLU → Linear(32 → 7).
  • Trainable Parameters: 53,703 parameters trained via Adam (lr = 0.001, weight decay = 1×10-5) with MSE loss.
Figure 5: Training and validation loss convergence curves for the 2-Layer Hybrid Residual GRU.

6. Autoregressive Multi-Step Trajectory Simulation

To validate the model for closed-loop Model Predictive Control (MPC), we simulated predictions autoregressively over rolling horizons from 1 to 20 steps (2 to 40 seconds into the future).

Figure 7: Reconstructed 2D horizontal trajectory comparing Actual Telemetry, Physics Baseline, ML-Only, and Hybrid Physics-GRU.

While the ML-Only model diverges due to compounding errors in recurrent feedback loops, the Hybrid model leverages kinematic bounding to preserve structural stability across multi-step forecast horizons.

7. Discussion & Failure Analysis

7.1 Dynamic State Superiority

The hybrid architecture achieved its most pronounced gains on variables dominated by hydrodynamic damping and restoring forces: Pitch (+15.48%), Depth (+12.45%), and Heading (+12.03%). Physics formulations assume instantaneous control surface action, whereas the GRU's recurrent hidden state effectively learns physical fin deflection delays and fluid restoring moments.

7.2 USBL Acoustic Measurement Noise & Position Overfitting

Horizontal coordinates showed slight error increases (-2.17% on North, -2.97% on East). As uncovered during our EDA, raw acoustic USBL fixes contain discrete high-frequency jumps caused by sound-ray refraction in ocean thermoclines. Neural networks trained with MSE loss inevitably overfit to these high-frequency measurement jumps rather than true vehicle motion.

Phase 1 Recommendation: Extended Kalman Filtering (EKF)
Applying an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) or RTS smoother to fuse high-rate DVL groundspeed with raw acoustic USBL fixes will eliminate non-physical position jumps before model training, rectifying coordinate overfitting.

8. Conclusion & Transition to Phase 2 (MPC)

Phase 1 demonstrated that combining a reduced-order kinematic physics model with a deep recurrent GRU residual network yields superior predictive accuracy while guaranteeing physical stability.

  • Phase 2 Objective: Embed the validated Hybrid Dynamics Model inside a receding-horizon Model Predictive Controller (MPC) to achieve optimal 3D path tracking.
  • Controller Benchmarking: Compare AI-MPC against tuned PID controllers on complex sinusoidal and 3D survey paths.
  • System Deployment: Integrate the FastAPI backend and browser simulation dashboard for real-time visualization.
